scenes.title: Getting started
scenes.learning_objective: Trace IP packets from sender through routers to receiver, distinguishing packet forwarding from TCP endpoint reliability.
scenes.narration_text: A sender carries TCP data inside IP packets. Routers inspect destination addresses and forward packets toward the receiver. They choose onward paths, while TCP at the endpoints manages a reliable, ordered stream of bytes for applications.

scenes.title: Following the changes
scenes.learning_objective: Distinguish forward IP packet delivery from reverse TCP acknowledgments sent by the receiving endpoint, not by routers.
scenes.relationship: The receiver's TCP endpoint acknowledges bytes; routers forward IP packets
scenes.narration_text: The receiving TCP endpoint sends an acknowledgment back toward the sender, indicating the next byte expected. This reverse acknowledgment also travels in IP packets through routers. Routers forward it; they do not acknowledge TCP data themselves.

scenes.title: Making connections
scenes.learning_objective: Explain how TCP sequence numbers, acknowledgments, and retransmission recover missing bytes and support ordered delivery.
scenes.narration_text: Sequence numbers identify byte positions. When acknowledgment progress stalls, a timeout can trigger retransmission of missing data. The receiver uses sequence numbers to restore order before delivering bytes to the application.

scenes.title: Putting it together
scenes.learning_objective: Summarize IP router forwarding versus TCP endpoint acknowledgments, retransmission, and ordered delivery.
bullets: TCP retries missing data and restores order
scenes.narration_text: To summarize, IP routers forward packets. TCP endpoints acknowledge received bytes, retry missing data, and provide ordered delivery. Forwarding and reliability have different responsibilities.
